name: Longest Unique Substring
background: A substring is a contiguous run of characters inside the given string. All characters in the run must be different to be valid.
task: Given a string, output the length of the longest contiguous substring that contains no repeated characters.
input_format: Line 1: a single string S (lowercase letters only)
constraints: 1 ≤ |S| ≤ 300000. S contains only characters 'a'–'z'. Expected O(n) solution.

name: Longest Unique ID Segment
background: A contiguous segment is a sequence of array elements with consecutive indices. All IDs in the segment must be pairwise distinct.
task: Given n integers (IDs), find the 1-based start and end indices of the longest contiguous subarray that contains no repeated ID. If multiple segments have the same maximum length, output the one with the smallest start index.
input_format: Line 1: integer n. Line 2: n space-separated integers (the sequence).
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 200000. Each ID is an integer between 0 and 10^9 inclusive. Expected O(n) time and O(n) memory.

name: Earliest Longest Color Run
background: A color run is a contiguous block of color names in the list. Names are tokens separated by spaces; a run is valid if every color in it appears at most once.
task: Given n color names, print the 0-based start and end indices (inclusive) of the earliest longest contiguous run that contains no repeated color.
input_format: Line 1: integer n. Line 2: n space-separated color names (each name uses only lowercase letters).
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 100000. Each color name is 1–10 lowercase letters. If multiple runs tie for maximum length, choose the one with the smallest start index. Expected O(n) time.

name: Max Unique Window Length (Numbers)
background: A contiguous subarray of numbers is a run of elements with consecutive positions. The run is valid if all numbers in it are distinct.
task: Given an array of integers, output the maximum length of any contiguous subarray that contains all distinct values.
input_format: Line 1: integer n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000. Each integer is between -10^9 and 10^9 inclusive. Expected O(n) time and O(n) extra memory.

name: Indices of First Longest Unique Run
background: A run is a contiguous substring of the input string. Characters are alphanumeric (letters or digits). A run is valid if no character appears more than once inside it.
task: Given a string of alphanumeric characters, output two integers: the 1-based starting index and the length of the earliest longest contiguous substring that contains no repeated characters.
input_format: Line 1: a single string S of alphanumeric characters (A–Z, a–z, 0–9).
constraints: 1 ≤ |S| ≤ 100000. S contains only alphanumeric characters. If multiple maximal runs tie, choose the one with the smallest 1-based start index. Expected O(n) time.

name: Minimum Substring Cover
background: A substring is a contiguous sequence of characters inside a string. A pattern is another string whose characters (with multiplicity) must all appear inside a substring to be considered covered.
task: Find the shortest substring of S that contains every character of T at least as many times as it appears in T. If multiple shortest substrings exist, return the leftmost one (smallest start index). If no such substring exists, print -1.
input_format: Line 1: string S (source). Line 2: string T (pattern). Both contain only lowercase letters.
constraints: 1 ≤ |S| ≤ 200000, 1 ≤ |T| ≤ 100000. All characters are 'a'–'z'.

name: Shortest Subarray Covering Multiset
background: A contiguous subarray is a sequence of consecutive elements of an array. A required multiset lists values and may include duplicates; the subarray must contain each listed value that many times.
task: Output two 1-based indices L and R for the shortest contiguous subarray of A that contains every value in the multiset M with at least the multiplicity given. If multiple solutions have the same length choose the one with the smallest L. If no subarray covers M print -1.
input_format: Line 1: two integers n m (n = length of A, m = number of items in multiset M). Line 2: n integers A1 ... An. Line 3: m integers (the multiset M values; values may repeat).
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 200000, 1 ≤ m ≤ 100000, each array value fits signed 32-bit integer. The multiset elements are arbitrary integers and may repeat.

name: Shopping List Window
background: A shopping sequence is the list of items encountered in order; an item name is a short word. A shopping list is a multiset of required items (items may repeat).
task: Find the shortest contiguous range of the shopping sequence that contains every item from the shopping list with at least the required multiplicity. Output two 1-based positions (start end). If multiple shortest ranges exist print the one with smallest start. If none exists print NOT FOUND.
input_format: Line 1: two integers k n (k = number of items in the shopping list, n = length of the store sequence). Line 2: k space-separated strings (the shopping list; items may repeat). Line 3: n space-separated strings (store sequence). Item strings contain only lowercase letters and no spaces.
constraints: 1 ≤ k ≤ 1000, 1 ≤ n ≤ 200000, each item string length ≤ 10. All words are lowercase letters. The shopping list items may include repeats.

name: Minimum A/B Cover
background: A substring is contiguous characters of a string that contains only the letters 'A' and 'B'. You are given required counts for 'A' and 'B' that the substring must meet or exceed.
task: Find the shortest substring of S that contains at least needA copies of 'A' and at least needB copies of 'B'. Output its 1-based start and end positions. If multiple shortest substrings exist return the one with smallest start. If none exists print -1.
input_format: Line 1: string S (only characters 'A' and 'B'). Line 2: two integers needA needB (required minimum counts for 'A' and 'B').
constraints: 1 ≤ |S| ≤ 200000. 1 ≤ needA ≤ |S|, 1 ≤ needB ≤ |S|. S contains only 'A' and 'B'.

name: Uppercase Letter Cover
background: A substring is a contiguous part of an uppercase-letter string. You are given a list of distinct uppercase letters and required counts for each; the substring must contain at least those counts for every listed letter.
task: Output the shortest substring of S that contains each required letter at least the specified number of times. If multiple shortest substrings exist choose the one with the smallest start index. If no substring meets all requirements print NONE. If a solution exists, output the substring itself.
input_format: Line 1: string S (uppercase letters A–Z). Line 2: integer t (number of distinct required letters). Next t lines: each line contains a character C and an integer k separated by a space (meaning letter C is required at least k times).
constraints: 1 ≤ |S| ≤ 200000, 1 ≤ t ≤ 26, for each requirement 1 ≤ k ≤ |S|. All letters are 'A'–'Z'. Required characters in the t lines are distinct.

name: Longest Substring With At Most K Distinct
background: A substring is a contiguous sequence of characters from a string. Distinct characters are the different letters that appear in the substring.
task: Given an integer k and a lowercase string S, output the length of the longest contiguous substring of S that contains at most k distinct characters. If no non-empty substring satisfies this (e.g., k = 0), output 0.
input_format:
Line 1: integer k
Line 2: string S (lowercase letters only)

name: Longest Product ID Run With At Most K Brands
background: A run is a contiguous subarray of product IDs. Distinct brands are the number of different ID values in the run.
task: Given n product IDs and an integer k, find the length of the longest contiguous subarray that contains at most k distinct ID values. If k = 0, output 0.
input_format:
Line 1: two integers n and k separated by a space
Line 2: n integers — the product IDs (space separated)
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000; 0 ≤ k ≤ n; each product ID is an integer in [0, 10^9]

name: Count Subarrays With At Most K Distinct Values
background: A subarray is a contiguous slice of the array. We count every contiguous subarray whose number of distinct values is at most k.
task: Given n integers and integer k, output the total number of contiguous subarrays whose number of distinct values is at most k. Empty subarray is not counted.
input_format:
Line 1: two integers n and k separated by a space
Line 2: n integers (space separated)
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000; 0 ≤ k ≤ n; each element is an integer in [−10^9, 10^9]

name: Longest Color Run With At Most K Colors
background: You are given a sequence of color codes (single uppercase letters). A run is a contiguous sequence of colors; distinct colors are the different letters in that run.
task: Given n color letters and integer k, output the length of the longest contiguous run that contains at most k distinct colors. If k = 0, output 0.
input_format:
Line 1: two integers n and k separated by a space
Line 2: n uppercase letters separated by spaces (each letter is 'A'..'Z')
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000; 0 ≤ k ≤ n; letters are 'A'..'Z'

name: Longest Time Window With At Most K Event Types
background: Events are recorded as integer type IDs in time order. A time window is a contiguous sequence of events; distinct event types are the different IDs inside the window.
task: Given n event type IDs and integer k, output the length of the longest contiguous time window that contains at most k distinct event types. If k = 0, output 0.
input_format:
Line 1: two integers n and k separated by a space
Line 2: n integers — event type IDs (space separated)
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000; 0 ≤ k ≤ n; each ID is an integer in [0, 10^9]

name: Exact Sum Subarray
background: You are given a list of positive integers. A contiguous subarray is a sequence of consecutive elements. Indices are 1-based.
task: Find any contiguous subarray whose elements sum exactly to S. If multiple exist, choose the one with the smallest left index; if still tied, choose the one with the smallest right index. Output the left and right indices separated by a space, or -1 if none exist.
input_format: Line 1: two integers n and S. Line 2: n positive integers a1 a2 ... an on one line.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000. 1 ≤ ai ≤ 10^9. 1 ≤ S ≤ 10^18. All ai are strictly positive. The chosen solution must run in O(n) time.

name: Count Exact-Sum Windows
background: Given a sequence of strictly positive integers, a contiguous window is any consecutive subsequence. Each valid window's sum is the total of its elements.
task: Output the number of contiguous windows whose sum equals S.
input_format: Line 1: two integers n and S. Line 2: n positive integers a1 a2 ... an on one line.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000. 1 ≤ ai ≤ 10^9. 1 ≤ S ≤ 10^18. All ai are strictly positive. Expected time O(n).

name: Shortest Exact Window
background: A contiguous window in a positive-valued array has a well-defined sum. Window length is the number of elements included.
task: Find the smallest length (number of elements) of any contiguous window whose sum equals S. Output that length, or -1 if none exists.
input_format: Line 1: two integers n and S. Line 2: n positive integers a1 a2 ... an on one line.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000. 1 ≤ ai ≤ 10^9. 1 ≤ S ≤ 10^18. All ai are strictly positive. Expected O(n) time.

name: Longest Exact Window
background: For a positive integer array, longer contiguous windows have larger sums in a monotone fashion when expanding the right end while left is fixed.
task: Find the maximum length of a contiguous window whose elements sum exactly to S. Output that length, or -1 if none exists.
input_format: Line 1: two integers n and S. Line 2: n positive integers a1 a2 ... an on one line.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000. 1 ≤ ai ≤ 10^9. 1 ≤ S ≤ 10^18. All ai are strictly positive. Expected O(n) time.

name: List Exact-Sum Starts
background: When a contiguous window sums to S, its starting index identifies where the block begins. Indices are 1-based.
task: List, in increasing order, all starting indices of contiguous windows whose elements sum exactly to S, separated by single spaces. If none exist, output -1.
input_format: Line 1: two integers n and S. Line 2: n positive integers a1 a2 ... an on one line.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000. 1 ≤ ai ≤ 10^9. 1 ≤ S ≤ 10^18. All ai are strictly positive. Expected O(n) time.

name: Subarray Sum Target
background: A subarray is a contiguous slice of the array. The sum of a subarray is the sum of its elements. Count every distinct pair of start and end indices (i ≤ j) that yields the required sum.
task: Given an integer array and a target T, count how many contiguous subarrays have sum exactly T. Output the count as a single integer.
input_format:
Line 1: n T (two integers)
Line 2: n integers a1 a2 ... an (space-separated)
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000. Each ai is between -1e9 and 1e9. |T| ≤ 1e18. The answer fits in a signed 64-bit integer.

name: Balanced AB Substrings
background: Treat 'A' as +1 and 'B' as -1. A substring is contiguous characters; its sum is the sum of mapped values. Balanced means equal counts of A and B, i.e., substring sum zero.
task: Given a string of A and B, count substrings whose number of A equals number of B. Output the count as a single integer.
input_format:
Line 1: n (integer length)
Line 2: string s of length n consisting only of characters 'A' and 'B'.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000. s contains only 'A' and 'B'. The answer fits in a signed 64-bit integer.

name: Exact Ones Segments
background: Given a binary array (0/1), the number of ones in a subarray is the sum of its elements. Count contiguous subarrays that contain exactly k ones.
task: Given n, k and an array of n zeros and ones, output the number of contiguous subarrays whose sum (number of ones) is exactly k.
input_format:
Line 1: n k (two integers)
Line 2: n integers (each 0 or 1) separated by spaces
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000. 0 ≤ k ≤ n. Each array element is 0 or 1. The answer fits in a signed 64-bit integer.

name: Robot Net Displacement
background: A string of '+' and '-' describes steps of +1 and -1 on a line. The net displacement of a contiguous interval is the sum of those steps.
task: Given n, target D and a string of '+' and '-', count contiguous intervals whose net displacement equals D. Output the count as a single integer.
input_format:
Line 1: n D (two integers)
Line 2: string of length n consisting only of '+' and '-'
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000. Each character is '+' or '-'. |D| ≤ 300000. The answer fits in a signed 64-bit integer.

name: Anomalous Periods
background: A time series of signed integers records successive changes. A contiguous period's total change is the sum of its values. We count periods equal to a given anomaly threshold.
task: Given n and a target T, count contiguous subarrays whose sum is exactly T. Output the count as a single integer.
input_format:
Line 1: n T (two integers)
Line 2: n integers b1 b2 ... bn (space-separated)
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000. Each bi is between -1e9 and 1e9. |T| ≤ 1e18. The answer fits in a signed 64-bit integer.

name: Balanced Bits
background: A contiguous substring is a block of adjacent characters. A balanced substring has exactly as many '0' characters as '1' characters.
task: Find the length of the longest contiguous substring with equal numbers of '0' and '1'. If no such substring exists print 0.
input_format: Line 1: n (integer), the length of the string. Line 2: a binary string of length n consisting of characters '0' and '1'.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000. The string contains only characters '0' and '1'. O(n) expected.

name: Red-Blue Pairs
background: A contiguous segment is a sequence of adjacent items in the string. Count every pair of start and end indices that form such a segment. Treat 'R' and 'B' as two opposite types.
task: Count how many contiguous segments have exactly the same number of 'R' characters as 'B' characters. Print the count as a single integer.
input_format: Line 1: n (integer), the length of the string. Line 2: a string of length n consisting only of 'R' and 'B'.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000. The string contains only 'R' and 'B'. Answer fits in a 64-bit signed integer. O(n) expected.

name: Match Period
background: You are given a sequence of scoring events. A contiguous period (subarray) is balanced if team A scored as many times as team B within that period.
task: Find a longest contiguous period where A and B scored equally. If multiple periods share maximal length, output the one with the earliest starting index. Print two 1-based integers: start and end index of that period. If none exists print "-1 -1".
input_format: Line 1: n (integer). Line 2: a string of length n made of characters 'A' and 'B', where character i is the team that scored on event i.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000. The string contains only 'A' and 'B'. O(n) expected.

name: Vowel-Consonant Balance
background: Vowels are the letters a, e, i, o, u. Every other lowercase English letter is a consonant. A contiguous substring is balanced if it contains exactly as many vowels as consonants.
task: Output the length of the longest contiguous substring with equal numbers of vowels and consonants. If none exists, print 0.
input_format: Line 1: n (integer). Line 2: a lowercase string of length n (letters 'a'–'z').
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000. The string contains only lowercase English letters. Vowels = {a,e,i,o,u}. O(n) expected.

name: Longest Equal Zero-One Blocks
background: A contiguous block (substring) is balanced when it contains exactly as many '0' characters as '1' characters. We care about the maximum possible length and how many distinct substrings achieve that length.
task: Find two integers: the length L of the longest contiguous substring with equal counts of '0' and '1', and the number of distinct substrings that achieve that length. If no balanced substring exists print "0 0".
input_format: Line 1: n (integer). Line 2: a binary string of length n consisting only of '0' and '1'.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000. The string contains only '0' and '1'. Use 64-bit for counts. O(n) expected.

name: Minimum Workdays
background: You have a list of positive daily workloads. A contiguous block of days is called a window and its value is the sum of workloads in that block. Only the sum and length of windows matter.
task: Find the minimum number of consecutive days whose total workload is at least the target S. If no such window exists, print 0.
input_format:
Line 1: two integers n and S separated by a space
Line 2: n positive integers (the workloads) separated by spaces
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000; 1 ≤ each workload ≤ 10^9; 1 ≤ S ≤ 10^18. All workloads are positive integers.

name: Shortest Batch To Reach Quota
background: A warehouse processes items in batches; each batch yields a positive quantity. Batches are listed in order and you may take only contiguous batches.
task: Output the smallest number of consecutive batches whose total quantity is at least the quota Q. If impossible, output 0.
input_format:
Line 1: two integers n and Q separated by a space
Line 2: n positive integers (quantities) separated by spaces
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000; 1 ≤ each quantity ≤ 10^9; 1 ≤ Q ≤ 10^18. All quantities are positive integers.

name: Snack Pack Minimum Span
background: Each snack pack has positive calories and packs are lined up. A span is a contiguous sequence of packs; its calories are their sum.
task: Determine the minimum number of consecutive packs whose calories sum to at least the required target T. Print 0 if no such span exists.
input_format:
Line 1: two integers n and T separated by a space
Line 2: n positive integers (calories) separated by spaces
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000; 1 ≤ each calorie ≤ 10^9; 1 ≤ T ≤ 10^18. All calories are positive integers.

name: Energy Boost Segment
background: You measure energy boosts provided by contiguous time intervals. Each interval value is positive and combined additively.
task: Find the shortest contiguous time interval whose total boost is at least the required amount R. If none exist, print 0.
input_format:
Line 1: two integers n and R separated by a space
Line 2: n positive integers (boosts) separated by spaces
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000; 1 ≤ each boost ≤ 10^9; 1 ≤ R ≤ 10^18. All boosts are positive integers.

name: Quick Supply Run
background: A delivery route has consecutive stops, each yielding a positive supply amount. A run is any contiguous group of stops.
task: Compute the minimum length of a contiguous run whose total supply is at least the demand D. Print 0 if no run meets the demand.
input_format:
Line 1: two integers n and D separated by a space
Line 2: n positive integers (supplies) separated by spaces
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000; 1 ≤ each supply ≤ 10^9; 1 ≤ D ≤ 10^18. All supplies are positive integers.

name: Longest Balanced Substring
background: A substring is a contiguous run of characters. The multiplicity of a character in a substring is how many times it appears there. An empty substring has length 0.
task: Find the length of the longest contiguous substring in which every character appears at most k times. If no non-empty substring satisfies this (for example k = 0), the answer is 0.
input_format:
Line 1: two integers n and k separated by space
Line 2: a string S of length n consisting of lowercase letters
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000; 0 ≤ k ≤ n; S contains only 'a'..'z'. Time limit expects O(n) solutions.

name: Warehouse Shelf Sequence
background: A contiguous window on a shelf is a contiguous sequence of product slots. Each product ID may appear multiple times in a window.
task: Find a longest contiguous window (subarray) where no product ID appears more than k times. Output the 1-based start and end indices of the leftmost such longest window. If the best length is 0, output "0 0".
input_format:
Line 1: two integers n and k separated by space
Line 2: n integers a1 a2 ... an separated by spaces
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000; 0 ≤ k ≤ n; each ai is a 32-bit signed integer. Time limit expects O(n) solutions using frequency counts and two pointers.

name: Event Log Filter
background: A contiguous subarray of events is valid if every event code appears at most k times inside it. We count non-empty contiguous subarrays.
task: Count how many non-empty contiguous subarrays of the sequence are valid (each event code appears ≤ k times). Output the count as a single integer.
input_format:
Line 1: two integers n and k separated by space
Line 2: n integers e1 e2 ... en separated by spaces
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000; 0 ≤ k ≤ n; each ei is a 32-bit signed integer. Answer may be up to n*(n+1)/2 (use 64-bit). Expected O(n) two-pointer solution.

name: Garden Path Distincts
background: A contiguous window is valid if every label in it appears at most k times. The distinct count is how many different labels appear in that window.
task: Among all longest valid contiguous windows, pick the leftmost one and output the number of distinct labels in that window. If the best length is 0, output 0.
input_format:
Line 1: two integers n and k separated by space
Line 2: n integers b1 b2 ... bn separated by spaces
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000; 0 ≤ k ≤ n; each bi is a 32-bit signed integer. Expect O(n) two-pointer + frequency map.

name: Playlist Repeat Limit
background: A playlist is a contiguous sequence of song IDs. In a valid playlist window no song ID appears more than k times.
task: Find a longest valid contiguous playlist window. Output two integers: its length and the song ID that has the highest frequency inside the leftmost such longest window (if several song IDs tie for highest frequency, output the smallest ID). If the best length is 0, output "0 0".
input_format:
Line 1: two integers n and k separated by space
Line 2: n integers s1 s2 ... sn separated by spaces
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000; 0 ≤ k ≤ n; each si is a 32-bit signed integer. Use O(n) sliding window; frequencies in the chosen window fit 32-bit.

name: Uniform Window Shift
background: You have a string of uppercase letters. A contiguous substring is uniform if every character in it is the same. Repainting a character means changing it to any other letter at unit cost.
task: Find the length of the longest contiguous substring that can be made uniform by repainting at most k characters. If multiple substrings tie, report the common length (tie-breaking not needed).
input_format: Line 1: Two integers n and k separated by a space. Line 2: A single string of length n consisting of uppercase letters A–Z.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 200000, 0 ≤ k ≤ n. The string contains only uppercase letters A–Z. Time limit expects O(n) or similar.

name: Color Stretch
background: You have a row of fence panels, each painted one of a small set of integer color IDs. Repainting a panel changes its color to any other integer color at unit cost.
task: Report the maximum length of a contiguous block of panels that can be repainted (at most k panels changed) so that the whole block has the same color.
input_format: Line 1: Two integers n and k separated by a space. Line 2: n integers c1 c2 ... cn separated by spaces, the color IDs of panels.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 200000, 0 ≤ k ≤ n. Color IDs are integers in the range 1..10. Time-efficient O(n) required.

name: Binary Block Fix
background: You have a binary string consisting of characters '0' and '1'. Repainting flips a character to the other bit at unit cost.
task: Compute the maximum length of a contiguous substring that can be made all '0' or all '1' by repainting at most k characters.
input_format: Line 1: Two integers n and k separated by a space. Line 2: A binary string of length n (characters '0' and '1').
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 200000, 0 ≤ k ≤ n. String contains only '0' and '1'. Expect O(n) solution.

name: Team Role Run
background: You are given a sequence of job-role labels (single words). A contiguous segment is uniform if every label in it is identical. Changing a member's role to any other label costs one repaint.
task: Find the maximum length of a contiguous segment that can be made to consist of a single role (any role you choose) after repainting at most k labels.
input_format: Line 1: Two integers n and k separated by a space. Line 2: n words separated by single spaces, each word is a label (no spaces inside labels).
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 200000, 0 ≤ k ≤ n. Each label is non-empty and contains no spaces; total input size fits usual limits. Expect O(n) with hashing or two-pointer counts.

name: Paint Target Strip
background: You have a strip of lowercase letters. You are given a specific target letter; repainting any character to any other letter costs one unit.
task: Given a target letter t, compute the maximum length of a contiguous substring that can be converted entirely to t using at most k repaints. Output that maximum length.
input_format: Line 1: Two integers n and k, and a single lowercase letter t, separated by spaces. Line 2: A lowercase string of length n.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 200000, 0 ≤ k ≤ n. The target t is a lowercase letter 'a'–'z'. The string contains only lowercase letters. Expect O(n) solution.

name: First At Least
background: You are given a sorted list of integers in non-decreasing order. The goal is to locate the earliest position where values reach or exceed a given target.
task: Output the smallest 1-based index i such that A[i] >= T. If no element is >= T, output -1.
input_format:
Line 1: n (number of elements)
Line 2: n space-separated integers A1 A2 ... An (non-decreasing)
Line 3: integer T (target)
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 200000. -10^9 ≤ Ai, T ≤ 10^9. A is sorted in non-decreasing order.

name: First Free Slot
background: A sequence of slots is represented by 0 (occupied) or 1 (free). The sequence is guaranteed to be monotone: all 0s (occupied) appear before any 1s (free).
task: Find the smallest 1-based index of a slot whose value is 1. If there is no 1, print -1.
input_format:
Line 1: n (number of slots)
Line 2: n space-separated integers S1 S2 ... Sn (each is 0 or 1, and the sequence is non-decreasing)
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 200000. Si ∈ {0,1}. Sequence is non-decreasing (zeros then ones).

name: First Failed Test
background: A sequence of test results is given as characters: 'P' for pass and 'F' for fail. It is guaranteed that once a test fails, all later tests also fail (all P's, then all F's).
task: Print the 1-based index of the first 'F'. If there is no failure, print -1.
input_format:
Line 1: n (number of tests)
Line 2: a string of length n consisting only of characters 'P' and 'F' (monotone: P*F*)
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 200000. The string matches the pattern P*F* (zero or more P then zero or more F).

name: Insert Position
background: Given a non-decreasing array, the insertion position for value x is the smallest index where x can be placed without breaking the order.
task: Print the insertion index i (0-based) which is the smallest i with A[i] >= x. If every element is < x, print n (append position).
input_format:
Line 1: n (number of elements)
Line 2: n space-separated integers A1 A2 ... An (non-decreasing)
Line 3: integer x (value to insert)
constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 200000. -10^9 ≤ Ai, x ≤ 10^9. A is sorted in non-decreasing order. (If n=0, the array line will be empty.)

name: First Day Cumulative Reaches
background: You have non-negative daily contributions. Cumulative sum by day d is the total from day 1 to d. The predicate 'cumulative >= M' is monotone in d.
task: Print the smallest 1-based day d such that the cumulative sum up to d is at least M. If M ≤ 0, the answer is 1. If the cumulative sum never reaches M, print -1.
input_format:
Line 1: n M (n and required cumulative target)
Line 2: n space-separated integers a1 a2 ... an (daily contributions, non-negative)

name: Last Value Not Above Target
background: You are given a sorted list of numbers in non-decreasing order. Indices are 1-based. A value is considered acceptable if it is less than or equal to a given target.
task: Find the largest index i (1-based) such that array[i] <= X. If no element satisfies this, output 0.
input_format: Line 1: two integers n and X. Line 2: n integers a1 a2 ... an (non-decreasing).
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000. Each ai and X is between -10^9 and 10^9. The array is sorted non-decreasing (a1 ≤ a2 ≤ ... ≤ an).

name: Last Reading Above Threshold
background: A sequence of sensor readings is given in non-increasing order (each reading is ≤ previous). Indices are 1-based. A reading meets the requirement if it is greater than or equal to a threshold.
task: Output the largest index i (1-based) such that reading[i] ≥ T. If no reading meets the threshold, output 0.
input_format: Line 1: two integers n and T. Line 2: n integers r1 r2 ... rn (non-increasing).
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000. Each ri and T is between -10^9 and 10^9. The readings are non-increasing (r1 ≥ r2 ≥ ... ≥ rn).

name: Last Prefix Within Budget
background: You are given a list of positive costs. The prefix sum up to index i is the total cost of the first i items. Indices are 1-based.
task: Find the largest index i (1-based) such that the sum of the first i values is ≤ S. If no prefix satisfies this, output 0.
input_format: Line 1: two integers n and S. Line 2: n positive integers c1 c2 ... cn.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000. 1 ≤ ci ≤ 10^9. 0 ≤ S ≤ 10^18. All ci are positive integers.

name: Last Character Not After Target
background: A string of lowercase letters is given in non-decreasing (sorted) order. Indices are 1-based. A character is acceptable if it is ≤ a given target character.
task: Return the largest index i (1-based) such that s[i] ≤ c. If no character satisfies this, output 0.
input_format: Line 1: integer n and a single lowercase character c separated by a space. Line 2: a string s of length n (sorted non-decreasing).
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000. s contains only 'a'..'z' and is sorted non-decreasing. c is a lowercase letter.

name: Last Start You Can Catch
background: You have a sorted list of candidate movie start times (minutes from 0). A movie runs for D minutes and must finish by minute 1439 (inclusive). Indices are 1-based.
task: Find the largest index i (1-based) such that start[i] + D - 1 ≤ 1439 (equivalently start[i] ≤ 1440 − D). If none qualifies, output 0.
input_format: Line 1: two integers n and D. Line 2: n integers t1 t2 ... tn (start times, non-decreasing).
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000. 1 ≤ D ≤ 1440. 0 ≤ ti ≤ 1439. The times are non-decreasing (t1 ≤ t2 ≤ ... ≤ tn).

name: Find Target Index in Rotated Array
background: A rotated sorted array is made by taking a strictly increasing list of distinct numbers and cutting it at one position then concatenating the two parts. Indexing is zero-based.
task: Given the rotated array and a target value, output the index (0-based) of the target if it exists, otherwise output -1.
input_format:
Line 1: n (number of elements)
Line 2: n space-separated integers (the rotated array)
Line 3: t (the target integer)
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000. All array values are distinct. The array is a rotation of a strictly increasing sequence. Values fit in signed 32-bit integers. Expected O(log n) time.

name: Find 1-Based Position in Rotated List
background: The list is a rotation of a strictly increasing sequence of distinct integers. Positions are counted starting at 1.
task: Output the 1-based position of the target in the given rotated list. If the target is not present, output -1.
input_format:
Line 1: n
Line 2: n space-separated integers (the rotated list)
Line 3: t (target integer)
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000. All values distinct. Array is a single rotation of a strictly increasing sequence. Values fit in signed 32-bit integers. Expected O(log n) time.

name: Membership Queries on Rotated Array
background: You are given a rotated sorted array with distinct values. Each query asks whether a given value appears in the array.
task: For each query value, print YES if it appears in the array, otherwise print NO. One answer per line in the same order as queries.
input_format:
Line 1: n
Line 2: n space-separated integers (the rotated array)
Line 3: q (number of queries)
Line 4: q space-separated integers (the queries)
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000. 1 ≤ q ≤ 300000. All array values are distinct. The array is a rotation of a strictly increasing sequence. Values fit in signed 32-bit integers. Each query must be answered in O(log n) for overall expected O((n + q) + q log n) performance.

name: Index of Smallest Element
background: The smallest element in a rotated strictly increasing array is the rotation pivot. Indices are zero-based.
task: Output the index (0-based) of the smallest element in the given rotated array.
input_format:
Line 1: n
Line 2: n space-separated integers (the rotated array)
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000. All array values are distinct and the array is a rotation of a strictly increasing sequence. Values fit in signed 32-bit integers. Expected O(log n) time.

name: Rightward Steps Between Two Values
background: Given a rotated array of distinct values, the rightward step count from position i to j is the number of moves increasing the index by 1 each time, wrapping to 0 after n-1. Positions are zero-based.
task: Given two integers a and b, output the number of rightward steps required to go from a to b (i.e., (index(b)-index(a) mod n), an integer between 0 and n-1). If either a or b is not present in the array, output -1.
input_format:
Line 1: n
Line 2: n space-separated integers (the rotated array)
Line 3: a b (two integers separated by space)
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000. All array values are distinct and the array is a rotation of a strictly increasing sequence. Values fit in signed 32-bit integers. Expected O(log n) time to locate each value.

name: Mountain Peak
background: A sequence of integer altitudes represents a single mountain trail: values strictly increase to one summit and then strictly decrease. Adjacent altitudes are never equal. Indices are 1-based (first reading is index 1).
task: Report the 1-based index of the summit (the element greater than its neighbors). If n=1 that element is the summit.
input_format:
Line 1: n (number of readings)
Line 2: n integers a1 a2 ... an (space-separated)
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000; each ai is an integer with |ai| ≤ 10^9; for 1 < i < n the sequence strictly increases up to a single peak and then strictly decreases (there is exactly one i with ai > ai-1 and ai > ai+1); adjacent values are never equal.

name: Loudest Moment
background: You have sampled sound levels (integers) over time. The samples strictly rise to one loudest moment then strictly fall; adjacent samples differ. Time indices start at 0.
task: Print the 0-based index of the loudest sample (the element greater than both neighbors). If n=1 that index is 0.
input_format:
Line 1: n
Line 2: n integers s0 s1 ... s{n-1} (space-separated)
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000; each sample is an integer with |si| ≤ 10^9; the sequence strictly increases to one maximum and then strictly decreases; adjacent values are never equal.

name: Profit Peak
background: Daily integer profits form a unimodal sequence: they strictly increase to a single best day then strictly decrease. Adjacent profits differ.
task: Output two integers: the 1-based day index of the best profit and the profit on that day, separated by a space.
input_format:
Line 1: n
Line 2: n integers p1 p2 ... pn (space-separated)
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000; each pi is integer with |pi| ≤ 10^9; profits strictly increase to exactly one peak and then strictly decrease; adjacent values are never equal.

name: Sensor Spike
background: A sensor produces at least three integer readings that strictly increase to a single spike and then strictly decrease; the spike is guaranteed not to be the first or last reading. Indices are 1-based.
task: Print the 1-based index of the spike reading (the element greater than its immediate neighbors).
input_format:
Line 1: n
Line 2: n integers r1 r2 ... rn (space-separated)
constraints: 3 ≤ n ≤ 300000; each ri is integer with |ri| ≤ 10^9; the sequence strictly increases to a single peak (which is not at index 1 or n) and then strictly decreases; adjacent values are never equal.

name: Unimodal Score Finder
background: A list of integer scores strictly increases to one top score then strictly decreases; neighbors are always different. You need the top score, not its position.
task: Print the integer value of the top (maximum) score.
input_format:
Line 1: n
Line 2: n integers v1 v2 ... vn (space-separated)
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000; each vi is integer with |vi| ≤ 10^9; the sequence strictly increases up to one maximum and then strictly decreases; adjacent values are never equal.

name: Find In Sorted Grid
background: You are given a rectangular grid of integers where each row is nondecreasing left-to-right and each column is nondecreasing top-to-bottom. Comparison is the usual integer comparison.
task: Decide whether the given target integer appears anywhere in the grid. Print YES if it appears, otherwise NO.
input_format: Line 1: Two integers R and C — the number of rows and columns. Next R lines: each line has C integers (the grid row). Last line: one integer — the target.
constraints: 1 ≤ R, C ≤ 300000, and R + C ≤ 300000. All grid rows are nondecreasing left-to-right and all columns are nondecreasing top-to-bottom. Grid values and target are integers in [-10^9, 10^9].

name: Coordinates of Unique Target
background: A matrix is given where each row is nondecreasing and each column is nondecreasing. 1-based row and column indices identify cells.
task: The target integer is guaranteed to appear exactly once in the matrix. Output two integers r and c — the 1-based row and column of the target. If multiple candidates could satisfy the search strategy, follow the deterministic rule that you must return the actual unique cell (there is exactly one).
input_format: Line 1: Two integers R and C. Next R lines: each line contains C integers (the matrix row). Last line: one integer — the target (guaranteed to occur exactly once).
constraints: 1 ≤ R, C ≤ 300000, and R + C ≤ 300000. Matrix rows and columns are nondecreasing. All values and the target are integers in [-10^9,10^9]. The target appears exactly once.

name: Any Match Position
background: A grid is sorted: each row is nondecreasing across columns and each column is nondecreasing down rows. You will follow a fixed corner-elimination movement starting at the top-right cell.
task: Using the deterministic corner-elimination rule starting at row=1, col=C: if current cell equals the target, print its 1-based coordinates (r c); if current cell > target, move left; if current cell < target, move down. Stop when you find the target or go outside the grid. If found, output the coordinates you arrived at; otherwise output -1 -1.
input_format: Line 1: Two integers R and C. Next R lines: each with C integers (the grid). Last line: one integer — the target.
constraints: 1 ≤ R, C ≤ 300000, and R + C ≤ 300000. Matrix rows and columns are nondecreasing. Values and target are integers in [-10^9,10^9].

name: Find Word In Lexicographic Matrix
background: Each cell contains a lowercase word. Rows are nondecreasing left-to-right and columns are nondecreasing top-to-bottom under standard dictionary (lexicographic) order.
task: Determine whether the target word appears. Starting at the top-right cell, compare lexicographically: if equal, print FOUND r c; if current > target, move left; if current < target, move down. If you exit the grid without finding the word, print NOT FOUND. Use 1-based coordinates.
input_format: Line 1: Two integers R and C. Next R lines: each line has C nonempty lowercase words separated by spaces. Last line: one word — the target.
constraints: 1 ≤ R, C ≤ 300000, and R + C ≤ 300000. All rows and columns are nondecreasing in lexicographic order. Words contain only lowercase letters and have length between 1 and 20. The target is a lowercase word.

name: Present or Absent (Negatives Allowed)
background: An integer grid is given where rows are nondecreasing and columns are nondecreasing. Values may be negative. Decide membership efficiently by eliminating rows or columns at each step.
task: Print PRESENT if the target appears in the grid, otherwise print ABSENT.
input_format: Line 1: Two integers R and C. Next R lines: each with C integers (the grid). Last line: one integer — the target.
constraints: 1 ≤ R, C ≤ 300000, and R + C ≤ 300000. Rows and columns are nondecreasing. Grid values and target are integers in [-10^18,10^18].

name: Next Greater Value
background: For each position in a list, the next greater value is the first later element that is strictly larger. If no such element exists, we use -1 as the marker.
task: Given n integers, for each element output the value of the first strictly greater element to its right, or -1 if none.
input_format:
Line 1: n (number of elements)
Line 2: n integers a1 a2 ... an separated by spaces
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 200000; each ai is an integer with -10^9 ≤ ai ≤ 10^9. The required solution runs in O(n) time and O(n) extra space.

name: Next Greater Distance
background: For each element the next greater distance is how many positions forward you must go to find the first strictly larger element. If none exists, report -1.
task: Given n integers, for each element output the positive distance (j - i) to the first later strictly greater element, or -1 if none.
input_format:
Line 1: n (number of elements)
Line 2: n integers a1 a2 ... an separated by spaces
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 200000; each ai is integer with -10^9 ≤ ai ≤ 10^9. Expected O(n) time and O(n) extra space.

name: Days Until Warmer
background: Each day's temperature is compared to later days; output how many days you must wait for a strictly warmer day, or 0 if none.
task: Given n daily temperatures, for each day output the number of days until a strictly warmer temperature occurs later, or 0 if none.
input_format:
Line 1: n (number of days)
Line 2: n integers t1 t2 ... tn separated by spaces
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 200000; each ti is an integer with -1000 ≤ ti ≤ 1000. Expected O(n) time and O(n) extra space.

name: Circular Next Greater Value
background: Treat the list as circular: after the last element you continue at the first. The circular next greater value for an element is the first strictly larger item encountered when scanning forward (wrapping at most once). If none exists, output -1.
task: Given n integers in a circular array, for each position output the first strictly greater value encountered later (wrapping allowed once), or -1 if none.
input_format:
Line 1: n (number of elements)
Line 2: n integers a1 a2 ... an separated by spaces
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 200000; each ai is integer with -10^9 ≤ ai ≤ 10^9. Expected O(n) time and O(n) extra space; at most one wrap-around pass is allowed.

name: Next Higher Price Index
background: For each price, the next higher price index is the first later position with a strictly larger price. Indices are 1-based; report 0 when there is no later higher price.
task: Given n prices, for each position output the 1-based index of the first later strictly larger price, or 0 if none.
input_format:
Line 1: n (number of prices)
Line 2: n integers p1 p2 ... pn separated by spaces
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 200000; each pi is integer with -10^9 ≤ pi ≤ 10^9. Expected O(n) time and O(n) extra space.

name: Nearest Previous Smaller Index
background: You are given a list of numbers. For each position, the nearest previous smaller index is the position of the closest element to its left that is strictly less than the current element. If there is no such element, we use 0.
task: For each position i (1-based), output the 1-based index of the nearest earlier element that is strictly smaller than a[i]. If none exists, output 0.
input_format:
Line 1: n (number of elements)
Line 2: n integers a1 a2 ... an
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000; each ai is an integer with |ai| ≤ 10^9. The answer must be produced in O(n) time and O(n) extra memory.

name: Left Span From Lower Boundary
background: For each day with a value, define the span as the number of consecutive days ending at this day since the last strictly smaller value to its left (inclusive of the current day). If no strictly smaller value exists to the left, the span equals the day index.
task: Output the span for each position i: span[i] = i - p where p is the 1-based index of the nearest earlier strictly smaller element; if none exists p = 0 so span = i.
input_format:
Line 1: n
Line 2: n integers a1 a2 ... an
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000; ai are integers, |ai| ≤ 10^9. Expected O(n) time and O(n) extra memory.

name: Height Of Left Lower Terrain
background: Given heights along a line, the left lower terrain for a position is the nearest earlier position whose height is strictly lower. If none exists, there is no left lower terrain.
task: For each position output the height of the nearest earlier element that is strictly smaller than this height; if none exists, output -1.
input_format:
Line 1: n
Line 2: n integers h1 h2 ... hn
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000; hi are integers with |hi| ≤ 10^9. Aim for O(n) time and O(n) extra memory.

name: Count Of Left Blockers
background: For each element, consider the consecutive elements immediately to its left that are not strictly smaller than it; stop when a strictly smaller element appears or the start is reached. The count of such consecutive left elements is the number of blockers.
task: For each position i output the count of consecutive earlier elements directly left of i that are ≥ a[i], i.e., the number of elements strictly between the nearest earlier strictly smaller index and i. (If there is no earlier strictly smaller element, count all elements to the left.)
input_format:
Line 1: n
Line 2: n integers a1 a2 ... an
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000; ai are integers, |ai| ≤ 10^9. Solutions should run in O(n) time and O(n) space.

name: Zero-Based Left Lower Index
background: For each element, the zero-based left lower index is the index (0-based) of the nearest earlier element that is strictly smaller. If none exists, we use -1.
task: Output for each position i (0-based indexing implied by outputs) the index of the nearest earlier element that is strictly smaller; output -1 if none exists. Use 0-based indices in your output.
input_format:
Line 1: n
Line 2: n integers a1 a2 ... an
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300000; ai integers with |ai| ≤ 10^9. Expected O(n) time and O(n) additional memory.

name: Daily Price Span
background: Each day has a price. The span on a day is how many consecutive days ending that day have prices less than or equal to that day's price (including the day itself).
task: For each day i (1..n) output the span: the number of consecutive days ending at i such that every day's price in that span is <= price[i]. Print n integers separated by spaces on a single line.
input_format:
Line 1: n (number of days)
Line 2: n integers p1 p2 ... pn (prices)

name: Cooling Streak
background: Each day has a temperature. A cooling streak ending on day i is a consecutive run of days ending at i where temperatures never increase when moving forward; equivalently, every previous day in the streak has temperature >= temperature on day i.
task: For each day i output the length of the longest contiguous streak ending at i where every day's temperature in the streak is >= temperature[i] (include day i). Print n integers separated by spaces on a single line.
input_format:
Line 1: n (number of days)
Line 2: n integers t1 t2 ... tn (temperatures)

name: Performance Drop Streak
background: Each contest has a rating. A drop streak ending at contest i is a contiguous run of contests ending at i where every previous rating in the run is strictly greater than rating[i].
task: For each contest i output the length of the longest contiguous streak ending at i where every previous rating in the streak is > rating[i] (strictly greater). Print n integers separated by spaces on a single line.
input_format:
Line 1: n (number of contests)
Line 2: n integers r1 r2 ... rn (ratings)

name: Upvote Reach
background: Each post has a number of upvotes. The reach on a post is how many consecutive posts ending at this one have fewer upvotes than the current post (strictly less).
task: For each post i output the number of consecutive posts ending at i such that each of those posts has upvotes < upvotes[i] (strictly less). Print n integers separated by spaces on a single line.
input_format:
Line 1: n (number of posts)
Line 2: n integers u1 u2 ... un (upvote counts)

name: Non-decreasing Run Lengths
background: A sequence is non-decreasing if every element is <= the next. The run length ending at i is the length of the longest contiguous segment ending at i that is non-decreasing.
task: For each position i output the length of the longest contiguous segment ending at i where each element is <= the next (i.e., arr[j] <= arr[j+1] inside the segment). Print n integers separated by spaces on a single line.
input_format:
Line 1: n (number of elements)
Line 2: n integers a1 a2 ... an

name: Kth Largest Score
background: You are given a sequence of numeric scores. The kth largest score is the value that would appear in position k if the sequence were sorted in descending order (largest first), counting duplicates separately.
task: Given n scores and an integer k, output the kth largest score among all n scores. If n < k, output NA. Ties count as separate entries (duplicates do not collapse).
input_format: Line 1: two integers n and k. Line 2: n integers s1 s2 ... sn (scores).
constraints: 1 <= n <= 200000; 1 <= k <= n; each score si is an integer with -10^9 <= si <= 10^9.

name: Kth Smallest After Each Insert
background: You receive numbers one by one. The kth smallest of a prefix is the value that would be at position k if that prefix were sorted in increasing order (smallest first).
task: Process the numbers in order. After each insertion i (1..n), if i < k print NA; otherwise print the kth smallest value among the first i numbers. Print one answer per line.
input_format: Line 1: two integers n and k. Line 2: n integers a1 a2 ... an (stream values).
constraints: 1 <= n <= 200000; 1 <= k <= n; each ai is an integer with -10^9 <= ai <= 10^9.

name: Top-K Replacement Count
background: As numbers arrive, the kth largest after a prefix is the value at position k when that prefix is sorted from largest to smallest (duplicates count separately).
task: Process the stream left to right. Each time the kth largest (once defined) differs from the kth largest after the previous element, that counts as a change. The first time the kth largest becomes defined (at the earliest prefix of size >= k) counts as one change. Output the total number of changes.
input_format: Line 1: two integers n and k. Line 2: n integers b1 b2 ... bn (stream values).
constraints: 1 <= n <= 200000; 1 <= k <= n; each bi is an integer with -10^9 <= bi <= 10^9.

name: Kth Lowest Latency Alarm
background: Each arrival is a measured latency. For a prefix, the kth smallest latency is the value at rank k when the prefix is sorted from smallest to largest.
task: Given threshold T, after each insertion report: UNKNOWN if fewer than k values have arrived; otherwise report ALARM if the current kth smallest is <= T, else OK. Output one token per line for each insertion.
input_format: Line 1: three integers n, k, and T. Line 2: n integers l1 l2 ... ln (latencies).
constraints: 1 <= n <= 200000; 1 <= k <= n; each li is an integer with -10^9 <= li <= 10^9; T is an integer with -10^9 <= T <= 10^9.

name: Prefix Queries for Kth Largest
background: A prefix of the stream contains the first p items. For a prefix, the kth largest is the value at position k when that prefix is sorted from largest to smallest; duplicates count separately.
task: Given q query indices p1..pq, for each query output the kth largest among the first p items, or NA if p < k. Output answers in the order queries are given, one per line.
input_format: Line 1: three integers n, k, q. Line 2: n integers v1 v2 ... vn. Next q lines: each line has one integer p (1 <= p <= n).
constraints: 1 <= n <= 200000; 1 <= k <= n; 1 <= q <= 200000; each vi is integer -10^9 <= vi <= 10^9; each query p satisfies 1 <= p <= n.

name: Merge Sorted Streams
background: You are given several sorted sequences of integers. Each sequence is static and sorted ascending. Treat each sequence as a stream where you can read and remove only the current first element (the head).
task: Merge all k sequences into a single nondecreasing sequence and output every element in order. When multiple current heads are equal, take the element from the sequence with smaller (1-based) index first.
input_format:
Line 1: k (number of sequences)
Lines 2..k+1: each line describes one sequence as: ni followed by ni integers (the elements of that sequence in increasing order).
constraints: 1 ≤ k ≤ 2000. For each i, 0 ≤ ni and all ni are integers. Total sum of all ni is between 1 and 200000. Each element is an integer between -1e9 and 1e9. All sequences are sorted ascending as given.

name: First M Smallest From Streams
background: You have k sorted (increasing) integer streams. You may repeatedly take the current smallest head from any stream. The streams are static and individually sorted.
task: Output the first m elements of the merged nondecreasing sequence. If m is larger than the total number of elements, output the whole merged sequence. When current heads tie, choose the smaller sequence index first.
input_format:
Line 1: k m (two integers)
Lines 2..k+1: each line: ni followed by ni integers (the elements of that sequence in increasing order).
constraints: 1 ≤ k ≤ 2000. 1 ≤ m ≤ 200000. For each i, 0 ≤ ni. Total sum of all ni is between 1 and 200000. Elements are integers in [-1e9, 1e9]. All sequences are sorted ascending.

name: Merged Sequence With Source Tags
background: Merge several sorted integer sequences into one by repeatedly taking the smallest current head. Tag each output element with which original sequence it came from (1-based index).
task: Produce the merged sequence as space-separated tokens of the form value:source where source is the 1-based index of the sequence the value came from. When heads are equal, take from the smaller sequence index first.
input_format:
Line 1: k
Lines 2..k+1: each line: ni followed by ni integers (sorted ascending).
constraints: 1 ≤ k ≤ 1000. For each i, 0 ≤ ni. Total elements between 1 and 200000. Elements are integers in [-1e9, 1e9]. Sequences are sorted ascending.

name: Merge And Remove Adjacent Duplicates
background: You merge multiple sorted integer streams by repeatedly taking the smallest head. After making the merged nondecreasing sequence, you compress any run of equal consecutive values to a single occurrence (i.e., remove adjacent duplicates).
task: Output the merged sequence after removing adjacent equal values. When heads tie, pick from the sequence with smaller index first.
input_format:
Line 1: k
Lines 2..k+1: each line: ni followed by ni integers (elements in nondecreasing order).
constraints: 1 ≤ k ≤ 2000. For each i, 0 ≤ ni. Total elements between 1 and 200000. Elements in [-1e9, 1e9]. Sequences are sorted ascending.

name: Median Of Merged Streams
background: Combine several sorted integer sequences into one multiset and consider the elements in sorted order. The median is the middle element (for odd total size) or the lower middle (for even total size).
task: Output the median value of the merged multiset. If the total number of elements is even, output the element at position total/2 (1-based lower median).
input_format:
Line 1: k
Lines 2..k+1: each line: ni followed by ni integers (sorted ascending).
constraints: 1 ≤ k ≤ 2000. For each i, 0 ≤ ni. Total number of elements is between 1 and 200000. Elements are integers in [-1e9, 1e9]. Sequences are sorted ascending.

name: Meeting Rooms Needed
background: Each meeting is an interval with an integer start and end time. An interval [s,e) is active at integer times t with s <= t < e (start inclusive, end exclusive).
task: Compute the minimum number of meeting rooms required so that every meeting can take place (i.e., the maximum number of meetings active at the same time). Output that single integer.
input_format: Line 1: n — number of meetings. Lines 2..n+1: two integers s and e (start and end) separated by space for each meeting.
constraints: 1 <= n <= 200000; 0 <= s < e <= 1e9 for every meeting; all values are integers.

name: Network Channel Peak Time
background: Each network request is an interval with integer start and end times. Here intervals are closed: [s,e] is active at integer time t when s <= t <= e. If one request ends at time t and another starts at t, they overlap at t.
task: Find the minimum number of channels needed (the maximum simultaneous requests) and the earliest integer time when that maximum first occurs. Output two integers: the count and the earliest time.
input_format: Line 1: n. Lines 2..n+1: two integers s and e (start and end) separated by space for each request.
constraints: 1 <= n <= 200000; 0 <= s <= e <= 1e9 for every request; all values are integers.

name: Airport Gates Duration of Peak
background: Each flight occupies a gate during an interval [s,e) (start inclusive, end exclusive). The airport needs enough gates equal to the maximum number of flights simultaneously occupying gates. The duration is measured as integer time units (end - start).
task: Output two integers: the minimum number of gates required (the maximum simultaneous flights) and the total integer duration during which the number of occupied gates equals that maximum (sum of lengths of all time segments where the occupancy equals the peak).
input_format: Line 1: n. Lines 2..n+1: two integers s and e (start and end) separated by space for each flight.
constraints: 1 <= n <= 200000; 0 <= s < e <= 1e9 for every flight; all values are integers.

name: Concurrent Requests (start + duration)
background: Each request is given as a start time and a positive duration. It occupies a resource during [s, s+d) (start inclusive, end exclusive).
task: Compute the minimum number of resources (servers) required so that all requests can be handled simultaneously. Output a single integer.
input_format: Line 1: n. Lines 2..n+1: two integers s and d (start and duration) separated by space for each request.
constraints: 1 <= n <= 200000; 0 <= s <= 1e9, 1 <= d <= 1e9, and s + d <= 1e9 for every request; all values are integers.

name: Subway Platforms and First Peak Train
background: Each train occupies a platform during [s,e) (start inclusive, end exclusive). Trains are listed in input order and numbered 1..n.
task: Output two integers: the minimum number of platforms required (the maximum simultaneous trains) and the 1-based index of the train with the smallest index that is present at the earliest time when that maximum first occurs. If multiple trains are active at that earliest peak time, choose the smallest index among them.
input_format: Line 1: n. Lines 2..n+1: two integers s and e (start and end) separated by space for each train (train 1 is the first of these lines, etc.).
constraints: 1 <= n <= 200000; 0 <= s < e <= 1e9 for every train; all values are integers.

name: Delivery Profits
background: Each job takes one whole day and has an integer money value and an integer last day by which it must be completed. You may do at most one job per day; days are nonnegative integers. A job with deadline d can be scheduled on any integer day x with 1 <= x <= d (if d = 0 it cannot be scheduled).
task: Choose a subset of jobs and schedule each on a distinct valid day so the total money is maximized. Output the maximum total money.
input_format: Line 1: n, the number of jobs. Lines 2..n: two integers per line, value and deadline (value deadline).
constraints: 1 <= n <= 100000. 0 <= value <= 10^9. 0 <= deadline <= 10^9. Sum of values fits in 64-bit signed integer.

name: Volunteer Shifts
background: Each volunteer shift takes one day. Each volunteer can work on any day up to their deadline day (a nonnegative integer). At most one volunteer can be assigned to a given day.
task: Assign volunteers to distinct valid days to maximize the number assigned. Output the maximum number of volunteers that can be scheduled.
input_format: Line 1: n, the number of volunteers. Line 2: n integers, the deadlines of volunteers (space-separated).
constraints: 1 <= n <= 100000. 0 <= deadlines[i] <= 10^9. Days are integers; a volunteer with deadline d can be assigned on any integer day x with 1 <= x <= d (if d = 0 they cannot be assigned).

name: Work Orders Selected
background: Each order takes one day and has a profit value and a deadline day. You may do at most one order per day; days are positive integers. If a deadline is 0 the order cannot be done.
task: Pick orders and schedule them so total profit is maximized. Then output the number of selected orders on the first line and, if that number is positive, output a second line with the 1-based indices of the selected orders in increasing order. If none are selected print only a single line with 0.
input_format: Line 1: n, number of orders. Lines 2..n: two integers per line, profit and deadline (profit deadline) in the input order (indices are 1..n).
constraints: 1 <= n <= 100000. 0 <= profit <= 10^9. 0 <= deadline <= 10^9. Use 1-based indexing when reporting order indices.

name: Festival Performances
background: Each performance lasts one day and has an integer fee and a last allowable day to perform. At most one performance per day is allowed. For tie-breaking, among schedules with equal total fee prefer choices that keep performers with smaller original input indices when possible (see replacement rule in task).
task: Select and schedule performances to maximize total fee. When considering replacing a currently selected performance with a new one of equal fee, replace only if the new performer has a strictly smaller input index (so smaller-index performers are preferred for equal fees). Output the maximum total fee.
input_format: Line 1: n, number of performers. Lines 2..n: two integers per line, fee and deadline (fee deadline), listed in the performers' input order (indices 1..n).
constraints: 1 <= n <= 100000. 0 <= fee <= 10^9. 0 <= deadline <= 10^9. Days are integers; a performer with deadline d can be scheduled on any day 1..d (d = 0 means cannot be scheduled).

name: Expired Coupons
background: Each coupon redeems a value and expires on a given day. Redeeming a coupon occupies that whole day and you may redeem at most one coupon per day. A coupon with deadline 0 cannot be redeemed.
task: Pick coupons to redeem so the total redeemed value is maximized. Output two integers: the maximum total value and the number of coupons redeemed.
input_format: Line 1: n, number of coupons. Lines 2..n: two integers per line, value and expiry day (value expiry).
constraints: 1 <= n <= 100000. 0 <= value <= 10^9. 0 <= expiry <= 10^9. Sum of values fits in 64-bit signed integer.

name: Jumping Across Stones
background: You stand on the first stone of a line of stones. Each stone has a number that is the maximum number of stones you may move forward in a single jump. You may only move forward or stay on the same or later stones (no backward moves).
task: Compute the minimum number of jumps required to land on the last stone. If you are already on the last stone, answer 0. If the last stone cannot be reached, output -1.
input_format:
Line 1: n (number of stones)
Line 2: n integers a1 a2 ... an (ai is the maximum forward jump length from stone i)
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 200000. 0 ≤ ai ≤ 10^9. Start on stone 1. Jumps move from index i to any j where i < j ≤ i + ai. Time limit encourages O(n) solutions.

name: Signal Relay
background: A line of communication towers is indexed 1..n. Each tower i can transmit a signal to any tower j where i < j ≤ i + ri. You start by transmitting from tower 1 and want to reach tower n using as few transmissions (hops) as possible.
task: Output the minimum number of transmissions (hops) needed to reach tower n from tower 1. If you are already at tower n, output 0. If tower n cannot be reached, output -1.
input_format:
Line 1: n (number of towers)
Line 2: n integers r1 r2 ... rn (ri is the maximum forward reach from tower i)
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 200000. 0 ≤ ri ≤ 10^9. Transmissions only move to strictly higher indices. Time limit encourages O(n) greedy expansion.

name: Checkpoint Marathon
background: Checkpoints are placed along a straight route at strictly increasing positions. From checkpoint i at position pi you can run forward up to distance di, i.e., you can reach any later checkpoint whose position ≤ pi + di. You start at the checkpoint at position 0 and want to reach the checkpoint at position L.
task: Given checkpoints including the start (position 0) and end (position L) in increasing order, output the minimal number of checkpoint-to-checkpoint moves needed to reach the checkpoint at position L. If you are already at L, output 0. If L cannot be reached, output -1.
input_format:
Line 1: m L (number of checkpoints and final position L)
Next m lines: each line has two integers: pi di (position and forward reach from that checkpoint)
(You are guaranteed p1 = 0 and pm = L, and p1 < p2 < ... < pm.)
constraints: 1 ≤ m ≤ 200000. 0 = p1 < p2 < ... < pm = L ≤ 10^9. 0 ≤ di ≤ 10^9. Moves only to later checkpoints. Expected O(m) greedy solution.

name: Mandatory Stop Jumps
background: You must travel forward across indexed positions 1..n. From index i you may jump to any index j where i < j ≤ i + ai. A list of mandatory indices must be visited; you must land exactly on each mandatory index in increasing order (the list includes index 1 and index n).
task: Compute the minimum total number of jumps needed to start at index 1, land on every mandatory index in order, and finish at index n. If you are already at index n and the list contains only 1, answer 0. If any required segment cannot be completed, output -1.
input_format:
Line 1: n k (number of positions and number of mandatory indices)
Line 2: n integers a1 a2 ... an (ai is the maximum forward jump length from i)
Line 3: k integers m1 m2 ... mk (mandatory indices in strictly increasing order; guaranteed m1 = 1 and mk = n)
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 200000. 1 ≤ k ≤ n. 0 ≤ ai ≤ 10^9. 1 = m1 < m2 < ... < mk = n. Time limit expects O(n) overall by processing segments greedily.

name: Road Repair Crews
background: Each crew can repair a continuous road segment starting at position si and extending up to si + li. You need to cover the entire road segment from position 0 up to position L (inclusive or beyond). Crews can be chosen in any order, but each chosen crew contributes its interval.
task: Find the minimal number of crews whose combined intervals cover every point from 0 to L. If L = 0, answer 0. If full coverage is impossible, output -1.
input_format:
Line 1: m L (number of crews and target length L)
Next m lines: two integers per line: si li (crew starting position and maximum repair length)
(Intervals are [si, si+li]. The lines may be in any order.)
constraints: 1 ≤ m ≤ 200000. 0 ≤ si ≤ 10^9, 0 ≤ li ≤ 10^9, 0 ≤ L ≤ 10^9. Covering is successful when the union of chosen intervals contains [0, L]. Expected O(m log m) or O(m) after sorting.

name: Project Tag Partitions
background: A list of task tags appears in chronological order. Each contiguous segment (partition) is a block of consecutive tasks. The goal is to cut the timeline so every tag appears in at most one block.
task: Split the sequence into the maximum number of contiguous blocks so that no tag appears in more than one block. If several maximum partitions exist, use the left-to-right greedy rule: scan from the start and close a block as soon as every tag seen inside it has no occurrences later. Output the lengths of the blocks in order, separated by single spaces.
input_format:
Line 1: integer n, the number of tasks.
Line 2: n tags separated by single spaces. Each tag contains only letters and digits, no spaces.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 200000. Each tag length is 1..10 characters. Total input size ≤ 1,000,000 characters. Tags may repeat.

name: Color Block Cuts
background: The line shows colored blocks by integer color codes in order. A cut separates contiguous blocks. Each color code must appear in at most one resulting piece.
task: Cut the sequence into the maximum number of contiguous pieces so each color appears in only one piece. Use the left-to-right greedy rule: close a piece as soon as all colors seen so far have no later occurrences. Output the lengths of the pieces in order, separated by single spaces.
input_format:
Line 1: integer n, the number of blocks.
Line 2: n integers (color codes) separated by single spaces.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 200000. Color codes are 32-bit signed integers. Total input size ≤ 1,000,000 characters.

name: Label Run Split
background: You are given a string of lowercase letters; each letter is a label on a position. A contiguous substring is a segment. Each label must belong to at most one segment.
task: Partition the string into the maximum number of contiguous segments so that each letter appears in only one segment. If multiple maximum partitions exist, close segments by scanning left-to-right and ending a segment as soon as all letters inside it have no later occurrences. Output the lengths of the segments in order, separated by single spaces.
input_format: Line 1: a nonempty string s of lowercase letters.
constraints: 1 ≤ |s| ≤ 200000. s contains only 'a'–'z'.

name: Robot Module Cuts
background: A production line lists part codes (single uppercase letters) placed in order. A module is a contiguous group of parts. No part code may appear in more than one final module.
task: Divide the list into the maximum number of contiguous modules so each part code appears in at most one module. If multiple maximum partitions exist, follow the left-to-right greedy rule: close a module when every code seen in it has no later occurrence. Output module lengths in order, separated by single spaces.
input_format:
Line 1: integer n, the number of parts.
Line 2: n uppercase letters separated by single spaces.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 200000. Each part code is a single letter 'A'–'Z'.
